disclaimer: This is general guidance only and is not a substitute for advice from a qualified agricultural extension officer or plant pathologist. Local regulations and approved practices may vary.
description: Red Rust on guava is caused by a parasitic green alga (Cephaleuros virescens) rather than a fungus or bacterium. It appears as slightly raised, velvety, orange-red or rust-coloured circular patches on the upper surface of leaves, and sometimes on stems and fruit. In warm and humid conditions the alga spreads easily. On its own it rarely kills a tree, but heavy infestations weaken the plant, reduce photosynthesis, and can damage young stems. It is commonly found on trees that are already stressed by poor nutrition or overcrowded canopies.
immediate_actions: Remove and destroy heavily infected leaves and stems — do not compost them.
Improve air circulation around affected trees through selective pruning of overcrowded branches.
Avoid excessive moisture on the leaf surface — adjust irrigation to keep foliage as dry as possible.
Check the overall health of the tree: poor nutrition and stress make trees more susceptible.
Consult a local agricultural extension officer for advice on approved algal management options if the infestation is severe.
spread_prevention: Prune trees regularly to maintain an open canopy and reduce the humidity that favours algal growth.
Avoid overhead irrigation — use drip or ground-level methods that keep the foliage dry.
Maintain adequate tree nutrition — healthy, vigorous trees are less susceptible.
Remove and destroy infected plant material promptly to reduce the source of spread.
Disinfect pruning tools between trees to prevent mechanical transfer.
long_term_monitoring: Inspect leaves and stems regularly during warm, wet seasons when the alga is most active.
Pay particular attention to the upper leaf surfaces where rust-coloured patches first appear.
Monitor overall tree vigour — repeated or worsening infestations may indicate underlying nutritional or drainage problems.
Consult a local agricultural extension officer if Red Rust is persistent despite improved canopy management.
